verify_reasons: Escort/pilot-car counts vary by highway type (two-lane vs multilane) per WAC 468-38-100; matrix below is simplified — confirm exact configuration per route
Overweight single-trip fee is a mileage/weight schedule (RCW 46.44.0941), not a flat fee; only the $14 minimum is codified here

superload_thresholds.note: WSDOT superload = non-divisible load exceeding 16' wide, 16' high, 125' load length, or 200,000 lbs. Over 200,000 lbs: apply at least 30 days ahead; over 16' wide/high: written application at least 7 calendar days ahead.

width.note: front pilot on two-lane undivided; rear pilot on multilane — see WAC 468-38-100
front and rear on two-lane; configuration varies on multilane
superload territory — escorts set case-by-case by WSDOT

length.note: rear pilot; rear overhang exceeding 1/3 of overall length also triggers a rear pilot

single_trip.fee_formula: Oversize-only (dimensional) single trip = $10 flat. Overweight = $14 minimum, scaled by excess weight and miles per RCW 46.44.0941 schedule (use WSDOT overweight fee calculator).
single_trip.note: Non-divisible loads only; most routine permits self-issuable online

annual.note: Annual permits are category-specific (e.g. single/double trailer divisible $100/yr, manufactured housing $360/yr); 30-day permits $10-$90 by type. No general-purpose annual OSOW permit.

movement_restrictions: Movement limited to one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset (Saturdays and Sundays included)
Loads not exceeding 12' wide, 14'6" high, and 105' long (including legal overhang) may move at night with proper lighting, Monday-Friday
notes: Superloads over 16' wide or 16' high require written application 7+ days ahead; over 200,000 lbs require 30 days
